name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (PM-USP CSSS)
summary: A merit-based Government of India scholarship for regular undergraduate and postgraduate students who did well in their Class 12 board exams, to help with day-to-day expenses while studying.
eligibility: Students who scored above the cut-off percentile in Class 12 board examinations and are pursuing regular degree courses at recognised institutions. A family income limit set by the scheme applies (check the current limit on the portal).
benefits: A yearly scholarship amount is paid directly to the student's bank account. The amount and duration are set by the scheme (check current figures on the portal).
documents_required: Proof of admission or enrolment from the institution
how_to_apply: Register and apply online on the National Scholarship Portal during the open application window, then get the application verified by your institution.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
summary: Financial support for Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10 so that money does not stop them from continuing their education.
eligibility: Students belonging to the Scheduled Caste category studying at post-matric level in recognised institutions. A family income ceiling set by the scheme applies (check the current limit).
benefits: Financial assistance that helps cover maintenance costs and certain compulsory fees, as per current scheme rules (check the portal for exact amounts).
how_to_apply: Apply online through the National Scholarship Portal or the relevant state scholarship portal, then submit the verification documents to your institution.

name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship for Girl Students
summary: A scholarship to encourage girls to pursue technical education such as engineering degrees and diplomas approved by AICTE.
eligibility: Girl students admitted to the first year of an AICTE-approved technical degree or diploma programme, including lateral entry to the second year. Limits on the number of girls per family and a family income limit apply (check current conditions).
benefits: Yearly financial assistance towards tuition and other education expenses for the duration of the programme (check current amount).
how_to_apply: Check the notification on the AICTE website and apply online, usually through the National Scholarship Portal, during the open window.

name: Vidya Lakshmi Education Loan Portal (including PM-Vidyalaxmi)
summary: A single online portal where students can see education loan schemes from participating banks and apply to several banks with one common application. PM-Vidyalaxmi, applied for through the same portal, supports students admitted to eligible top-ranked institutions.
eligibility: Indian students who have secured admission to a recognised higher education institution. PM-Vidyalaxmi has extra conditions such as institution ranking and family income limits for interest support (check current rules).
benefits: One application for loans from multiple banks. PM-Vidyalaxmi offers collateral-free, guarantee-backed loans up to a set limit and interest support for eligible low-income families (check current terms).
documents_required: Co-applicant (parent or guardian) KYC and income documents
how_to_apply: Register on the Vidya Lakshmi portal, fill the common education loan application, choose banks, and track the application status online.

name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
summary: A government skill training programme offering short-term courses with assessment and certification to help young people gain job-ready skills.
eligibility: Indian youth as defined by the scheme guidelines, often those who are unemployed or school or college dropouts. Age and education requirements differ by version (check the current guidelines).
benefits: Training at approved centres, assessment, and a government-recognised skill certificate. Earlier versions also gave monetary rewards on certification (check the current version).
how_to_apply: Find an approved training centre and course on the official skill portal, then enrol with the centre.

name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
summary: An income support scheme that gives eligible farmer families Rs 6,000 per year, paid directly to their bank account.
eligibility: Landholding farmer families as defined by the scheme. Some categories, such as institutional landholders and higher-income taxpayers, are excluded (check the exclusion list on the official site).
benefits: Rs 6,000 per year, paid in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 by direct bank transfer.
how_to_apply: Register through the Farmers Corner on the PM-KISAN website, or through a Common Service Centre or the local agriculture office, and complete e-KYC.

name: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
summary: A health insurance scheme that provides cashless hospital treatment at empanelled public and private hospitals for eligible families.
eligibility: Families identified through the scheme's socio-economic criteria. Eligibility is checked against government records; you can verify it on the official site or at an empanelled hospital help desk.
benefits: Health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation, with cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals.
documents_required: Ration card or family identity document
how_to_apply: Check eligibility on the official PM-JAY site, then get your Ayushman card made at a Common Service Centre or an empanelled hospital help desk.

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
summary: Collateral-free loans for small, non-farm, income-generating businesses such as shops, small manufacturing, and services, given by banks and financial institutions.
eligibility: Indian citizens with a business plan for a non-farm income-generating activity in manufacturing, trading or services, needing credit within the scheme limit.
benefits: Loans up to Rs 10 lakh in three categories: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishore (Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh) and Tarun (Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh). Limits may be revised, so check the current terms.
how_to_apply: Apply at a bank, NBFC or microfinance institution, or through the online loan portal linked from the official MUDRA site.

name: Stand-Up India
summary: A scheme that helps Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs get bank loans to set up a new enterprise.
eligibility: SC/ST and/or women entrepreneurs above 18 years setting up a first-time new (greenfield) enterprise. For non-individual businesses, at least 51 percent ownership and control must be with SC/ST or women. The applicant should not be in default to any bank.
benefits: Bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore for a new enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading, or allied agriculture activities.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Stand-Up Mitra portal, or directly at a bank branch, or through the Lead District Manager.
